title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: Scenic AVL #7: Scott Mountain
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
There is very limited parking at the [trailhead](https://maps.app.goo.gl/fETct2fiMiLz1HEG8). Please plan to meet at Lake Hills Church parking lot at 10 minutes before the start to condense cars.
We will meet in the parking lot area close to the intersection of Lake Drive and Black Midge lane.

Lake Hills Church Parking Lot is pictured above.
- [https://maps.app.goo.gl/X1TctrhYv3gihmh66](https://maps.app.goo.gl/X1TctrhYv3gihmh66)
*Call the hike leader at 828-290-0886 if you cannot find us. Do not text.

**Rating**: Moderate
**Elevation**: 800
**Distance**: 5 miles
**Surface**: Trail
**Pace**: 3 mph
**Dogs**: on leash.
**Gear**: Long pants recommended, bug spray, water. The ticks are bad on this trail. Bring your bug spray !
**Features**: wooded trail, interesting plants and fungi. Bears are shy, but we may see them, also deer and squirrels. 3 miles uphill, 2.25 down.
**All Trails Route**:
[Scott Mountain Loop on AllTrails](https://www.alltrails.com/explore/map/scott-mountain-loop-4217403?p=-1&sh=ifwm3x)

[Scenic Asheville Series](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1XUm-X1_OhxKIi8JU5rhjsW37cAl4yYx8yB_NEjjI5Lk): there are 9 hikes in the series, plus a few wild cards. a hike , even if you are on the waiting list .

**Guests**: Make sure your guests are fit enough to complete the hike. if someone is a guest, their hike will not count toward a badge because there will not be a record of their name .

title: The Art of Sound Healing
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
We welcome you to Asheville Art Museum to embrace the fullness of the fall season, to turn inward, root into stillness, and shed what no longer serves us. This morning sanctuary at the Museum offers space to rest, quiet the mind, and dream new intentions into existence. We will use breathwork, meditation, and a 50-minute sound bath to let go of old habits, attachments, and grief, and to drop deep into a state of profound, restorative rest. 
Sound baths promote deep release and relaxation, entraining our brainwaves to shift into a dreamlike state. This gentle, grounding practice is open to everybody—no experience needed. Come as you are, tired or wired, or somewhere in between. Please bring a yoga mat or pad, along with anything else to make you comfortable, like cushions and blankets. 
About the Instructor
Timothy Burgin is a world music percussionist who has spent more than 20 years collecting and playing sound healing instruments. A Kripalu & Pranakriya-trained yoga instructor who has lived and taught in Asheville since 2004, he has completed more than 500 hours of yoga training and founded YogaBasics.com. He leads sound baths throughout Asheville, drawing on his training in acupuncture, bodywork, yoga energetics, anatomy, and physiology. 
Register Now 
What are the Benefits to Sound Bowl Healing Music?
Sound bowl healing music involves the use of crystal or Tibetan singing bowls that produce harmonic vibrations. These vibrations are believed to promote deep relaxation, reduce stress, and support emotional and physical healing. The sound frequencies can help align chakras, calm the nervous system, and create a meditative state conducive to mindfulness and inner peace.

title: A Halloween Walk at the John C. Campbell Folk School in Brasstown NC
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
The John C. Campbell Folk School is located in Brasstown, Clay County, NC. It has classes in over 50 subjects, including art, craft, dance, music, and nature. (My wife took lap dulcimer lessons there many years ago. A family friend teaches there regularly.) This is the place where John Jacob Niles first performed a song he had collected, "I Wonder as I Wander".

We will gather in the main parking lot of the campus. Our first stop will be at Keith House, where there are restrooms. We will go to the Craft Shop, follow some trails, visit the Herb Garden, see the Eagle Dancer Sculpture, and past a kiln. This is one walk where we will definitely not hesitate to stop and look at various things there are to see. Your camera is a must on this one.

Our route is 5 KM/3.1 miles. Tennis shoes are fine, as there is no significant elevation change. Most will not want walking sticks (although I plan to take one). Bring a protein snack and plenty of water. Wheelchairs might have a somewhat hard time, but trail strollers should be ok. If I remember, dogs would probably be ok.

Before you leave, you may want to pick up lunch at the Folk School. You might bring a picnic lunch from home. Or you might catch some lunch after you have left campus and are on your way home.

title: Cemetery Loop Tr; a Saunter
description:
Hendo Fun Friends
**A Walk in the Park;**
**This Week: *Cemetery Loop Tr:***
**DESCRIPTION;**
*The Cemetery Loop Trail is a pleasant and short footpath which, when combined with the nearby Long Branch Trail offers a quick loop hike into a lesser-visited corner of Pisgah National Forest. Along the way there’s a decent variety of habitats to be seen. The main attraction is the 19th Century Cemetery which it passes at its far eastern extremity. Named the McCall Cemetery, it is named for the family and descendants of Samuel McCall who settled nearby in the late 1700’s. The cemetery sits in a serenely beautiful spot at the base of a low pine covered ridge.*
Remember - hikes led by ‘the Curmudgeon’ tend to have pleasant surprises.

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

title: Samhain: A Creative Journey through Autumn’s Threshold
description:
Samhaim: A Creative Journey through this Threshold of Autumn
with Catherine Willows 
Saturday, October 31  |  10 am – 1 pm 
Register Here!
Samhain marks a sacred threshold—the earth releases what is no longer needed, and the Northern Hemisphere begins its descent into the darkness, turning its energy inward toward the stillness of winter to come. We too are invited to slow down, turning our attention toward the transitions and endings that have shaped our lives through this passing year. This is a season of mystery and the unknown, time to discover what may be hidden beneath the surface: deeper knowing, unexpected beauty, new perspectives, and possibilities that have yet to reveal themselves. 
Together, we will attune to Nature and this sacred season within the Arboretum gardens, listen to the deeper rhythms moving through us, and invite our intuition into the creative process. Through expressive artmaking, we will enter this mid-autumn threshold and explore the mystery it holds. Artmaking becomes the portal through which we enter the mystery. Creativity becomes the elixir through which alchemy can open into discovery and transformation. 
No artistic experience is needed, only curiosity, a willingness to listen inwardly, and an openness to discover what reveals itself. If you have a journal, bring that with you to use during the class but all other supplies will be provided. 
Catherine Willows is a Registered Nurse, Certified Functional Medicine Health Coach, and Transformational Creativity Coach, and founder of Willows Coaching and Consulting. While holding sacred space, she guides adults in awakening their inner creativity — moving beyond the demands of daily life into greater flow, self-discovery, and joy through intuitive art-making processes. Catherine believes creativity and our connection to the natural world are deeply interwoven — both vital pillars of wellbeing, supporting nervous system regulation and inner equanimity, and together essential for living a meaningful, embodied life aligned with purpose and authentic expression.

title: Jazz Brunch w/ “Four Peanuts” trio
location: French Broad River Brewery, 101 Fairview Rd, Asheville, NC, United States
description:
Jazz Brunch is now officially on the schedule for every Saturday here in the taproom! We’re so very excited to introduce our newest free weekly event, open to all ages, family & pet-friendly





If you haven’t experienced Jazz Brunch yet, here’s what you can expect: from the moment the music begins, the taproom fills with that perfect weekend energy… laid-back jazz, fresh brunch plates, great beer, and a room full of people settling in and staying awhile. Friends gather around tables, conversations flow easily, and the rhythm of the music sets the tone for a perfect, easy Saturday. It’s exactly the kind of atmosphere we hoped to create when this idea first came to life!



We’re especially excited to continue working with our house Jazz band, “Four Peanuts”, whose smooth, soulful sound brings everything together. The group explores both original compositions and zesty covers of tunes you may or may not know. The trio features Alex Taub on keyboards, Brennan Dugan on bass, and Joe Enright on drums, and will certainly leave your peanuts salted and boiled to perfection! Their music pairs effortlessly with the relaxed brunch setting, turning an ordinary morning into something memorable. The all-new brunch menu is absolutely something to be excited about! French Broad River Pizza will be serving up a mix of breakfast and lunch favorites designed to pair perfectly with a chill afternoon in the taproom.






Thank you for supporting live music, local artists, and community gatherings here at French Broad River Brewery. We can’t wait to welcome you back to the taproom… brunch plate in one hand, beer in the other, and jazz in the background.


  
French Broad River Brewery is more than just a place to enjoy a drink—it’s a community hub where great beer, delicious pizza, live music, and good times come together. Just minutes from the Biltmore Estate & Downtown, our taproom is a gathering spot for locals and visitors alike. We regularly host live music and entertainment in our taproom, making French Broad River Brewery a lively hub of local activity. From bluegrass to reggae, there’s always something happening. Check out our Events Page to see what’s coming up next! 
No brewery experience is complete without great food. That’s why we offer French Broad River Pizza, serving up hot, hand-tossed pizzas made to order. Whether you’re here for a quick slice or a full meal, our pizza perfectly complements our craft beers and the lively atmosphere of our taproom. frenchbroadbrewery.com/pizza

description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.



Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.



The five women comprising Nobody’s Darling each have a long history of playing old-time music. Individually they have played in many other bands through the years, including The Carolina Oldtimers, The Pegtwisters, The Zuma House Band, Too Hot To Cook, The Luke Smathers Mountain Swing Band, Honey Holler, and The Carolina Chick Peas.



Stop in to enjoy the music and an afternoon libation or two, perhaps with an early supper or light bite . . . and don't forget your dancing shoes!

description:

Sunday, November 1st
1st Dance Wave 8:30\-10:30am \| Warmup 8:30am \| Opening Circle 9am
2nd Dance Wave 10:30\-12:30am \| Warmup 10:30am \| Opening Circle 11am
Auxiliary Facilitator Eduardo Arias

Intention: Who Lights The Sun

Everything is vibration. Every atom, every heartbeat, every thought hums at its own frequency. And light is what lets a frequency rise.
We look up at the sun and assume it burns on its own.
But nothing shines alone. Somewhere below, a single ember sends its warmth upward in a thousand quiet threads. Each thread is a signal, a pulse of energy that lifts the sun higher. The sun is only as bright as the light it receives.
We are the same. We don’t climb to a higher frequency by force. We get tuned there by light: a person who sees us clearly, a sound that cracks something open, a moment of stillness, a memory that still glows. Light carries everything a body needs to vibrate higher. It brings warmth, clarity, direction, and the courage to keep burning when the world goes dark.
Without it, we fall quiet. With it, we resonate.
This wave is for the ember behind your sun. It’s for the source you rarely name but always feel. Follow the threads down and you’ll find it.
Then ask yourself, and mean it: who lights you?
And whose sun are you lighting?

title: South Arts: Southern Circuit Tour of Independent Filmmakers | They Dream
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Join us for a screening of They Dream followed by a conversation with the filmmaker, William D. Caballero. 
After 20 years of chronicling his Puerto Rican family, a director and his mother craft animations that bring their loved ones back to life. 
 
Screening time: 1:26:00 
RESERVE TICKETS NOW 
About the filmmaker:
William D. Caballero is an American filmmaker whose work merges documentary, animation, and handcrafted miniature worlds to explore memory, migration, faith, and the emotional architecture of family. Across film, television, and short-form media, Caballero has developed a singular visual language rooted in tactile set-building, intergenerational storytelling, and a deep reverence for his Puerto Rican heritage. In 2001, he was awarded the prestigious Gates Millennium Scholarship, recognizing his academic promise and leadership at an early stage in his career. Bachelor of Fine Arts from Pratt Institute in 2006 and a Master of Arts from New York University (NYU) in 2008. 
This foundation in both fine art and cinematic storytelling laid the groundwork for a practice that bridges visual art, documentary realism, and experimental fabrication. While at NYU, Caballero created American Dreams Deferred, his first (but not last) autobiographical feature about his family. Caballero first gained widespread recognition in 2015 as the creator of the HBO series Gran’Pa Knows Best, which premiered on HBO and ran for two seasons. Centered on 3D-printed miniature recreations of his Puerto Rican grandfather, the series combined playful scale with emotional depth, redefining what personal storytelling could look like on television. Its inventive approach to memory and intergenerational dialogue positioned Caballero as a bold new voice in hybrid nonfiction storytelling.

title: Birding for Beginners
description:
Birding for Beginners
with Shane Myers 
Tuesday, November 3  |  9 – 10:30am 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
Join us on this birding walk around the NC Arboretum gardens and trails in search of our most colorful residents. We will go over best practices for using binoculars, recommendations for purchasing your own binoculars, and popular field guides to use. Bring your own binoculars but if you do not have a pair we have some loaner binoculars available to use during the program. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Shane Myers’ interest in nature began as a child with a love of dinosaurs. This quickly grew to include fossils, insects, and reptiles, and learning from the notes his grandparents kept of the birds that came to their feeders in Toledo, Ohio.  He has a Bachelors of Science in Wildlife Biology and did most of his undergraduate work on dragonflies and damselflies. He’s assisted in outreach and education for plant conservation groups, Odonata Groups, and various bird groups. Shane currently works for the Adult Education department at the NC Arboretum.

title: Butter Gap Loop; a Saunter
description:
Hendo Fun Friends
We will begin behind the fish hatchery up the Cedar Rock Tr, visit only 1 Cedar Rock Falls side trails, visit the abandoned beaver dam pond, connect with the Butter Gap and return downhill on the (newly developed mountain bike friendly) Buttergap switchbacks. Heavily forested ‘natural' surface with occasional rock & roots.
Up to 12 ppl are welcome to join us. Remember - hikes led by ‘the Curmudgeon’ tend to have pleasant surprises.
Difficulty: All the climb is in the 1st half of the loop. Bridges cross the streams. The downhill from the high point is constant. **Popular mountain biker section.**
**Geriatrics are asked to bring their own BP cuffs.**

***https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bf5TgVRGND4***

description:
Awakening Asheville
Whether you've never set foot in a Spirited Improv circle or you've been coming home to us for years, I want to let you know about something new. A single playshop, just two hours, where you can feel the magic for yourself or simply enjoy it again with fresh eyes.

What if one day could remind you what it feels like to be fully human, together?

**What is Spirited Improv "Try it out" Playshop?**
A 2-hour playshop of movement, music, story, and unscripted connection. No script, no performance pressure, no experience needed. Just a circle of people willing to show up, play, and see what unfolds when a room lets go of the need to get it right.

**When?**
Nov 3rd, 12:00-2 pm in Montford

**Who it's for**
People craving real connection, creative expression, and a little more Love in their lives. If you're drawn to personal growth, spiritual community, or simply want an evening that feels different from the ones that came before it, this is for you.

**Led by**
Jessica Chilton, an expressive arts practitioner and TEDx performer with twenty years in improvisational performing arts. She holds space with warmth and a deep trust in whatever wants to emerge in the room.

**What people are saying**
"It's like free-falling into the unknown, but with a big, warm, and fluffy safety net that hugs you when you land."
"We're just taking off all our stuff and walking out in our essence."
Come see for yourself.

description:
Crokinole Tuesdays at Highland Brewing Taproom
Join us every Tuesday in the Taproom for an evening of flicks, strategy, and friendly competition! We’re hosting the Asheville Crokinole Club—a community of players who love this classic dexterity board game. 
Never played? No problem! Crokinole is easy to learn and endlessly fun. Players take turns flicking wooden discs across a circular board, aiming for the high-scoring center zones. The twist? If your opponent has discs on the board, you must hit one—miss, and your piece is out! 
Whether you’re a seasoned pro or just curious, come grab a pint, meet new friends, and test your skills.

title: AVL Digital Nomads - Book Club
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**November 2026 Selection - *Klara and the Sun* by Kazuo Ishiguro**
[Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/dp/059331817X) - [GoodReads](https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/54120408-klara-and-the-sun)

*Here is the story of Klara, an Artificial Friend with outstanding observational qualities, who, from her place in the store, watches carefully the behavior of those who come in to browse, and of those who pass on the street outside. She remains hopeful that a customer will soon choose her. Klara and the Sun is a thrilling book that offers a look at our changing world through the eyes of an unforgettable narrator, and one that explores the fundamental question: what does it mean to love?*

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-

**Welcome to our monthly Book Club!** We’re a small, friendly group that gets together for fun, thoughtful conversations about a different book each month.

Finished the whole book? Great. Only made it through a few chapters? Still come. Didn’t read it at all but the discussion sounds interesting? Honestly, you’re welcome too.
We meet on the **first Tuesday of every month**.

One of the best things about this group is that we keep it relatively small and guide the conversation, so it doesn’t turn into three people talking while everyone else quietly questions their life choices. Everyone has a chance to jump in, share their thoughts, and explore the book’s characters, themes, writing, and bigger ideas.

You definitely don’t need to be a literary expert. Whether you read constantly or you’re trying to get back into it, this is a relaxed place to discover new books, hear different perspectives, and meet some great people along the way.

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: Shut Up & Write event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

HOSTS: This is a multi-host event, so most of the time there will be a host present. If we are unlucky and no host can attend, please find each other and self-organize. Pay attention to the event chat and comments to see who is available.

WI-FI: Yes!

PARKING: Street parking in metered spots is free after 6pm. Closest municipal garages ($2/hour) are Wall St. & Coxe Street/Sears Alley.

Every atom in your body was forged in the belly of a dying star. title: The Polyvagal Sangha
description:
Inner Peace Collective
**The Polyvagal Sangha**
*A community of seekers exploring nervous system regulation through the lens of ancient wisdom and modern science.*

A new tribe is forming. We're inviting 30 like-minded and like-hearted folks into an ongoing inquiry — learning to cultivate a greater felt sense of calm, ease, safety, and resilience in our bodies, our relationships, and the world around us. The goal isn't just personal regulation, but a ripple effect of co-regulation: a shift in how we show up for others and move through our own lives.

This is the first class in a 3-class series. The whole is greater than the sum of its parts, yet a single dive will yield beneficial results towards salutogenesis.

**Teachers:** Omri Sitton, D.C. and Wills Reed, LCMHCA

**Cost:** $10–$15 suggested donation to local nonprofit *Source Of Wellness*.
\*No one is turned away for lack of funds — all donations are appreciated.

**How to Reserve Your Spot** (please do both — priority goes to folks who complete both steps):

1. **Text Omri at 828-298-0011** with your name and whether you'd like to pay via Venmo or at the door
2. **RSVP on Meetup** using the button on this page

*A note on the two-step process: based on past events, people who only RSVP on Meetup often don't show up. Texting Omri directly helps us plan for who's actually coming — so please do both.*

**A Bit More Detail:**
Polyvagal Theory (PVT) — conceptualized by Stephen Porges — reveals how our body and brain collaborate to respond to everyday stress and deeply held trauma. It highlights the role of the autonomic nervous system, especially the vagus nerve, in shaping our physical and mental health. Paired with mindfulness practices drawn from ancient traditions, PVT offers us both the science and the felt experience of coming back to our center.

By building community together, we naturally stimulate the social engagement system — the nervous system's highest branch — fostering connection, safety, and ease in body, mind, and life. This is the essence of The Polyvagal Sangha.

**Participants will learn:**

* Polyvagal Theory's three defining principles
* Somatic activities specific to each branch of the autonomic nervous system
* Awareness practices to soften emotional triggers and past traumas
* The body's innate biological responses, and the role of mindfulness in being present to "what is"
* How connecting with others committed to personal growth naturally lifts and supports us all

Join Omri and Wills for a series of illustrated, experiential presentations that will inspire your spirit, engage your mind, and challenge your creativity — as you uncover the enormous potential of applying this work in your daily life.

*Feel Well. Heal Well. Live Well.*

**About the teachers:**

**About Omri**
Omri Sitton, D.C., Cert. ZB has 25 years of experience in multiple fields of the healing arts. His passion in helping others has a strong emphasis on self-care.

He naturally weaves the connection between mindfulness practice, cellular consciousness, and polyvagal theory into his experiential classes.

Dr. Omri practices Tonal Chiropractic, Zero Balancing, and Polyvagal Touch in Asheville, offering what he refers to as ChiroSomatics.
Learn more at [omsourcewellness.com](https://www.omsourcewellness.com/)

**About Wills**
Wills Reed, LCMHCA, is an Asheville-based psychotherapist with a particular interest in how our earliest relationships, life experiences, and nervous systems shape the way we experience ourselves and others.

His work draws from attachment-focused therapy, EMDR, somatic approaches, and a longtime personal practice of meditation and contemplative traditions. He enjoys helping people translate these ideas into practical experiences of greater safety, connection, and freedom in everyday life.

Let's face it, we’ve all got something. A recurring frustration, an exhausting pattern, an issue we’ve tried to resolve a dozen different ways that somehow keeps showing up.

This is a fresh approach to them—a way to quit working on the same old problems and start outgrowing them.

**If you could wave a magic wand, what pattern or obstacle in your life would you make disappear? Bring it here.**

*“The greatest and most important problems of life are all in a certain sense insoluble. … They can never be solved, but only outgrown.”*
*— Carl Jung*

Join fellow ADN member Rachel Bulkley, founder of The WellBeing Project, for an interactive workshop on a different approach to the problems that keep us stuck.

Together, we’ll look under the hood of what makes life suck right now. Or, if you prefer, the specific sources of annoying friction in your otherwise perfectly delightful existence.

We’ll look at the difference between repeatedly trying to solve our problems and tending the conditions underneath them.

**Who it's for**

* You’ve tried all the stuff: books, practices, therapy, new routines—and still feel like something isn’t clicking.
* You’re turned off by elite coaching claims and trendy self-help programs, but you’re interested in understanding yourself and growing healthier.
* You’re curious about human behavior, the conditions that help us thrive, and why knowing what to do doesn’t always translate into doing it.
* You enjoy thoughtful conversations with interesting people. Especially when you leave seeing something differently.

**What we'll do**
We’ll kick off with 15 minutes to mingle, then get to work. This is an active workshop, so come with one persistent problem, pattern, or source of frustration in mind.

We’ll start with a brief grounding exercise, then take an honest look at how you’ve approached your obstacle so far.

From there, we’ll step back and look at:

* Some common beliefs about success, effort, and care that may be making life unnecessarily difficult.
* The fundamental needs all humans share, and what happens when those needs go unmet.
* How The Ten Areas of Human Needs can help us understand what’s underneath our recurring struggles.
* What becomes possible when we start tending the conditions that support our growth.

Then we’ll return to the obstacle you brought with you and see what looks different. We’ll leave time at the end for questions, and you’re welcome to stick around and socialize after.

**What you'll leave with**

* A fresh perspective on a familiar challenge.
* A clearer understanding of what might be underneath it.
* A practical approach to creating healthier conditions in your life.
* A way of thinking you can apply to other recurring struggles.

**A few things...**
Your privacy is yours. Most of the reflection happens in your own notebook. You’re welcome to contribute to the discussion, but nobody will be asked to disclose personal details.

**Bring:** A notebook, a pen, an open mind, and one frustrating thing you’d happily wave goodbye to.

**Getting there:** We’ll meet in Room 5 at Hatch Coworking, 45 South French Broad Ave, Asheville. Free parking is available behind the building. Before the event, you’ll get a note with parking and entry details.

**Come as you are. Bring your obstacle. Let’s see what we can unkink.**

title: WNC Sierra Club 11/4: The Conservation Power of Art
description:
WNC Sierra Club
Mark your calendars for our Nov. 4 program about the conservation power of art, featuring local artist Spencer Beals and Doc Varn of Preserving a Picturesque America.

**Spencer Beals** is an Asheville-based artist and community organizer. He has been making art in the River Arts District full-time for the last four years despite losing his life’s work in Hurricane Helene. He continues to host Sketchbook Club, Nature Journaling Club and conservation based art and storytelling events.

**Doc Varn** will talk about his work with the nonprofit Preserving a Picturesque America (PAPA) to continue the tradition of using the power of the arts to preserve and conserve across the country. He will share stories and visuals of how they find the exact locations where artists of the 1800s created the art that inspired the creation of state and national parks across America. Once rediscovered, regional artists create modern depictions of these locations to share how things have changed, sometimes in triumph and sometimes sharing our mistakes.

The WNC Sierra Club meets monthly in Room 102 at UNCA’s Reuter Center on Campus Drive and simultaneously on [Zoom](https://unca-edu.zoom.us/j/85189349413?pwd=QmorsXPwjbS0BgiLR7xLItF3M1atab.1).

**Parking at UNC Asheville:** If you do not have a parking sticker from OLLI, you'll need to register for parking either ahead of time at [unca.aimsparking.com](unca.aimsparking.com) or at the Reuter Center on the night of the meeting. The latest information about fees and requirements can be found at that link. There are no visitor fees after 5 p.m.

About this Event
"Caring for myself is not self - indulgence; it is self-preservation, and that is an act of political warfare." Audre Lorde

This is an invitation specifically for persons who identify as Black or African American and are overwhelmed with the injustice of the world and are ready to create space in their lives for self-care as we fight for justice for all! (We offer a parallel session for Allies to connect, learn and find support in their work to dismantle racism at allies.eventbrite.com)

We believe Black people deserve a space to relax, reassess, and realign ourselves.

We are a collective of Black stress-management & wellness instructors inspired by human values.

We are here to facilitate your journey of trauma-relief and stress-management.

Imagine how much more energy you will have and how much more powerful you will be when you cut your stress levels in half!

And it can be done in just a few minutes using nothing but your own breath...

Over the last 10 years, we've taught over 100,000 people to do just that.
The key is that your breath is directly linked to your emotions.

-Open, safe space for sharing and self-care for Black people

Led by Black facilitators, certified in stress and trauma relief.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Graybeard Falls -- 6 mi, 1,200 ft. gain
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
**PLEASE READ ENTIRE DESCRIPTION BELOW**

**Sign-up opens Sunday, Nov. 1st at 8 PM**

The Mt. Graybeard Trail is a favorite of many, myself included. We’ll do an out-and-back, around 3 miles up and the same coming back. There's a clearing by Graybeard Falls where we'll take a short break before heading down.

Because of a sustained uphill segment and lots of heads-down walking over roots & rocks, this hike earns a solid 5.0 difficulty level on a 10-point scale. If you ever use hiking poles, they'd be useful here. Parts of the uphill are definitely not in the "easy" category, so if you're a less experienced hiker and unsure whether you're okay with 1,000'+ in elevation gain, it's best to sit this one out rather than risk holding back the group. We'll move at a fairly good pace, averaging around 2.2 mph.

There are three stream crossings. One via a relatively new bridge, and the other two require some rock-hopping. The trail can be muddy in parts, too, so wear good hiking shoes.

***Dog Policy:*** Dogs are welcome but must be leashed.

***Guest Policy:*** If you'd like to bring a guest, they'll need to join the Asheville Hiking Group and sign up for the hike on their own. Alternatively, if you've made it onto the "Going" list, contact me in advance to check whether it's okay to bring a "+1". Depending on timing and demand, we may be able to add your guest.

**MEET-UP TIME & PLACE**

Parking at the trailhead is very tight, so carpooling is a must. We'll meet at the **Black Mountain Ingles at 550 Route NC-9, which is near Exit 64 off I-40.** We'll **leave promptly at 8:45,** so please arrive early for check-in and organizing rides.

We’ll gather at the **north end** of the Ingles parking lot toward McDonald's (but not in the McD's lot), which is toward the right when you enter the Ingles lot. Look for my car, a silver Hyundai sedan.

On Google Maps: **[https://bit.ly/3TLR4yG](https://bit.ly/3TLR4yG)**

**COURTESY TO WAIT-LISTERS**
Only sign up if you definitely plan to come. If you must cancel, please change your status to "Not Going" as soon as possible so wait-listers can have sufficient notice. And please please PLEASE don't be a no-show.

If you're on the waiting list, keep checking through the evening before the hike. We often get last-minute dropouts. Also, if you know at some point that you won't be able to attend even if someone drops out, please remove yourself from the waiting list.

**WEATHER**
I'll watch the weather and post a cancellation message by 7:30 AM if the forecast is >50% chance of precipitation.

**QUESTIONS?**
You can message me through MeetUp until 8:30 AM the day of. Cell reception may be sketchy, but you can try to text me up to the start of the hike: (803) 767-3094.

**LEGALESE**
This Asheville Hiking Group event involves hiking and, possibly, transportation to and from the meetup site. Participants are responsible for their own safety and affirm that they have the appropriate skills, physical conditioning, equipment, and supplies. Hiking may involve risks to oneself and property. Neither your hike organizer nor Asheville Hiking Group can assure your safety nor eliminate all risks. Participants assume full responsibility for any injuries, damages, or losses.

title: Handmade Holiday: Paper Pamphlets, mighty little books
description:
Handmade Holiday: Paper Pamphlets, Mighty Little Books
with Joyce Tromba 
Friday, November 6  |  10am – 1pm 
Register Here!
In this class you will learn how to make one of the easiest and most versatile book structures: the pamphlet.  This book goes all the way back to the 4th century as one of the earliest ways to secure paper and documents. We will explore three different variations of this and look at even more possibilities that are easy to do once you know the basic technique. All materials will be provided in this class. 
Joyce Tromba is happily settled into life in lovely Western North Carolina after living and teaching around the world for 30 years. Her travels have exposed her to many fiber traditions and she has always found groups of fiber folks wherever she was to share her making with. Joyce has 20+ years teaching design, sewing, knitting, quilting and bookmaking to High School students and adults. She has studied fiber and book and fiber arts at Penland, Arrowmont, John C. Campbell Folk School, and the Center for Book Arts in New York City. Her work can be found at Local Cloth where she also teaches natural dyeing, bookmaking and sewing classes.

A miracle is a shift in perception from fear to Love.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

description:
Asheville Cuddle Collective
Please note- If you want to attend this event you need to purchase a ticket- We advertise in many places and only paid tickets will reserve your space. use the link below to reserve your ticket-

What is a Sensual Snuggle Event?\*\*
This is a sweet & welcoming event where we practice and use verbal consent to connect and share touch. We talk about boundaries and practice both saying and receiving a “no”. In this space it is common to see people cuddle, share massage, have their hair brushed, kiss, expose nipples, play, laugh, cry, and be vulnerable. This is a sober space where we can relax and connect with other humans who are seeking touch based connection.
We strive for this to be a safe event. Safe touch enhances our ability to connect with and trust people. When we are in a space of safety, we are able to relax, feel comfort, and be vulnerable.

**Our Agreements:**
1- We ask for what we want an wait for a yes before touching others.
2- We say no if we don’t want to do something.
3- We try to receive a no with grace and not take it personally.
4- We arrive on time, clean (as scent free as possible), and sober.
5- We keep our pants/shorts on at this event. (Tops are optional; this is a sensual space, not a sexual space.)
6- We are here to connect with others. Connection can be verbal, platonic, or spicy!
7- We welcome diversity. Isms and Phobias are not welcome here!

**Who should attend:**
People who are interested in safely exploring touch and sensuality with strangers. This includes people who are single, people who are not single, couples, folks who are new to town and looking for connection, people of all/any genders and sexual orientations, people of all ages (18 and up). People who understand and respect consent, who will take care of themselves and people around them. This event is queer-normative. The guest list will include all genders, orientations, ages, and personalities. If that’s not your thing… This is not the event for you.
***Who should NOT attend:***
-People who are only looking for a sex party.
-People who do not understand and respect consent.
-People who have extreme fear of setting and speaking their personal boundaries; in order to create a safe space we need to know that you will say “no” if you feel a no.
-People who are homophobic, racist, sexist, ageist, ableist…
-People under 18 years of age.
***Schedule of the Evening***

\*6:50pm Doors Open, Mix & Mingle

* 7:00pm We gather in a circle to meet each other, build a container, cover consent and boundary setting and discuss event agreements. Then we will play a few intimacy building games to meet and connect with other people in the room. Please make sure you arrive on-time!
\*8:15pm Once the container is built we will have self directed snuggling and sensual interactions until the end of the party.
* 10:50pm Closing Circle; a time to re-center and connect as a group to verbally share anything that came up at the event or to voice gratitude to someone(s) you enjoyed interacting with.
\*11:00pm cleanup & head home; you are welcome to help.

**We take individual and group safety seriously!** If you experience, see, or know that one of our participants is not safe to be at this event we want to know about it. We are committed to doing our best to create a safe environment which means that if someone is causing harm (physical or mental) that person is not welcome here (this includes harm that takes place outside of our events). We stand behind survivors and know that some of our participants are here to heal from touch based trauma.

These events are not "gender balanced"[. Check out our website for more information about this decision.](http://holdmeavl.com/why-i-dont-gender-balance-events/)

**Simple definitions/clarifications-** Platonic- marked by the absence of romance or sex.
Most of the interactions we have with friends and strangers are platonic.
Sensual- gratification of the senses or the indulgence of appetite.
We might feel sensual when we feel someone's breath on our neck or experience a extra long and slow caress.
Sexual- having or involving sex.
Often involving one more more peoples genitals; perhaps seeking orgasm.

Asheville Movement Collective
Friday, November 6th
Evening Dance Wave 7:00 pm \- 9:00 pm \| Warmup 7pm \| Opening Circle 7:30pm
Facilitator DJ SeigeA (CJ O'Reilly)

Intention: Ensemble: Within and Beyond...

Your first dance partner is yourself.

The second is the floor.
But between those two; an infinite array of partners:
your body - its joints, tendons, muscles...
your mind - its thoughts, memories, imaginings...

And beyond that, the music... another dancer... Third... fourth.. beyond!

Start from that first... work with each partner... listen deeply, and find your way to an integrated ensemble.

## About DJ SeigeA (CJ O'Reilly)

CJ O'Reilly has been creating ecstatic dance waves for the Asheville community since 2014. Their eclectic mix of musical styles beckons dancers into new patterns of movement and expression through diverse time signatures and instrumentation, and a wide range of musical and emotive qualities. CJ's waves explore high peaks, beautiful vistas, juicy lowlands and the profound reflective stillness of tranquil water. CJ's dance waves are pre-produced and refined through the body and ears of a dancer and audiophile.
Find more of DJ SeigeA's dance waves at [https://dj.seigea.com](https://dj.seigea.com)

If you are unfamiliar with the Camino, here are a few links to learn more:
[American Pilgrims on the Camino](https://americanpilgrims.org/iwpmap_directory/western-north-carolina/)
[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Way_(2010_film)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Way_(2010_film))
This route is inspired by the Camino Primitivo, which has more hills than most of the other routes to Santiago de Compostela.

**Start:** 9:00 AM. Please arrive 10 minutes early.
**Meeting Place:** Ingles, 915 Merrimon Ave at the corner of Beaverdam Rd; meet in the corner of the parking lot near the Ingles sign and near Beaverdam Rd. Restrooms are available.
**Full Distance:** 10.7 miles
**Shorter Options:** 6, 7, or 8 miles
**Elevation Gain:** 1560 feet
**Duration:** Allow 6 hours with lunch stop
**Hike Leader:** Maurice Frank
**Overview:**
This challenging high elevation gain walk is inspired by the Camino Primitivo. We begin and end at Ingles on Merrimon Avenue and Beaverdam Rd.
Our first stage is a warm up on rolling hills through the beautiful heavily wooded Sherwood Heights neighborhood. Crossing over via Windsor Rd we reach the Reynolds Mountain community. We stop to rest, hydrate and have a snack.
In the next section we steeply ascend up and around the top with beautiful long-range views. After lunch at The Village Porch in Reynolds Mountain we return around the back of Beaver Lake.
There are several options for a shorter less strenuous walk of about 6, 7, or 8 miles. The Sherwood Heights hills are moderate and you can skip the climb up Reynolds Mountain.
There is no coffee stop along the route, and no actual restrooms. We pass porto potties outside homes being renovated or constructed.
Almost all of the route is on pavement. Wear appropriate shoes and being snacks and water.

**Guests:** For this hike, there are no guest restrictions. Bring them with you.

The organizer of this trip is a volunteer and not a professional guide. The function of the organizer is only to organize this trip. title: Nov 7th Morning Community Cuddles
description:
Asheville Cuddle Collective
Please note- If you want to attend this event you need to purchase a ticket- We advertise in many places and only paid tickets will reserve your space. **[Click HERE to reserve your ticket!](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/nov-7th-morning-community-cuddle)**[ ](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/nov-7th-morning-community-cuddle)

**This is a non-sexual touch based event that invites participants to explore platonic intimacy in a safe environment** with like-minded people. We respect personal boundaries and through a supportive framework of mutual agreements that maximize safety and create a space of easy openness and compassionate connection.
At this event we have the chance to normalize touch with clear boundaries; this is a space for respectful, consent-based touch. We allow ourselves to be seen. We have fun.
We welcome people of all backgrounds, genders, ethnicities, relationship styles, sexualities, sizes, and ages (18+).

**THE RULES**

1. Clothes stay on for the whole event.
2. You do not have to touch anyone at this event.
3. You must receive a verbal YES before you touch anyone.
4. Take care of yourself and those you choose to interact with.
5. Speak up if you have a question, concern, or if you need assistance with anything during the event.
6. All emotions are welcome- we love vulnerability.
**WHY CUDDLE?**
Touch is a basic human need, and many of us do not get enough; most people don’t even know they are missing touch, or have a way to ask for touch without sexualizing it. We believe deeply in the power of touch, and the importance of communication and consent in creating a safe space for touch.
CUDDLING WITH STRANGERS
Cuddling with strangers sounds weird or scary to most people. “Will I like it?” “What if someone wants to touch me and I don’t want to?” “What if I say yes and it’s not what I want?” “What if I really want to touch someone and they say no?” These are all normal questions. The answer is that this is a space created to ask for exactly what you want, and receive NOTHING you don’t want. Many people start out nervous at a cuddle event & most are really glad they came.

**Schedule:**
6:50-7pm: Arrive with snacks to share! Get comfortable, meet, mingle, & snack.
7:05pm: Welcome Circle- its mandatory. We will set our container, talk about personal boundaries, communication, & consent.
7:15pm: Icebreakers and connective activities.
8:00pm: Open cuddling! You MUST ask and get a verbal ‘yes’ before touching or cuddling with anybody at this event. If you are not sure how to do this – great! – we will talk about it during the welcome circle.
10:50pm: Closing Circle, cleanup and head home.
**ETIQUETTE**

\*ARRIVE ON TIME: It is important that all participants arrive before the Welcome Circle. The Welcome Circle serves the purpose of creating the safe space for consensual, non-sexual touch between participants and making sure that everyone is informed about consent.

* Please arrive clean & as scent free as possible.
\*BE SOBER: Please do not drink or smoke before or at this event.

**WHAT TO BRING:** personal water bottle and snacks to share, a friend, a date – whatever cuddle accessories you like! The only thing that you are required to bring is a clean and sober you.

These events are not "gender balanced".

**We take individual and group safety seriously!** If you experience, see, or know that one of our participants is not safe to be at this event we want to know about it. We are committed to doing our best to create a safe environment which means that if someone is causing harm (physical or mental) that person is not welcome here (this includes harm that takes place outside of our events). We stand behind survivors and know that some of our participants are here to heal from touch based trauma.

\*refund policy-
Full refund if you cancel 7 days before the event or you cancel due to illness, emergency, or direct exposure to covid/flu.
Credit towards a future event if you cancel more than 3 days before an event.
No refund if you cancel within 2 days of the event or no-show.

title: Sacred Forests of the World
description:
Sacred Forests of the World
with Alison Ormsby 
Saturday, November 7  |  1 – 3 pm 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
This class will explore the biological and cultural aspects of areas around the world that are conserved due to local beliefs and traditions.  Sacred natural sites include forests, mountains, and springs that have cultural significance.  Some sites also have taboos on use of species within the areas, which serves a conservation function.  Most are not government-protected lands; rather, are managed by local committees, caretakers and/or religious leaders. Specific examples and research from India, Ghana, and Sierra Leone will be shared. Participants will discuss possible connections to forests in Western North Carolina. 
Alison Ormsby has a PhD in Environmental Studies and is a human ecologist with 30 years of experience working with people and protected areas, environmental education, and sacred natural sites. Alison publishes topics that relate to the interaction of people and nature, including sustainable communities, wildlife policy, citizen science, sustainable tourism, and ethnobotany.  Her research focuses on conservation of sacred forests globally.

with Lauren Lampley

Ever wondered how you can identify a tree without its leaves? All tree species have different patterns of bark and leaf/flower buds that can be used to identify them even in winter time. In this program, we will look closely at the common trees around the NC Arboretum trails and point out specific characteristics of their buds and bark so you can identify them even without their leaves. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time.

She currently works at the NC Arboretum as the Adult Education Coordinator managing all the programming hosted through the Adult Education Department.

title: Forest Bathing Retreat: Gratitude and Reciprocity
description:
Forest Bathing Retreat: Gratitude and Reciprocity
with Christal Hebal 
Saturday, November 7  |  2 – 5 pm 
Register Here!
“Paying attention is a form of reciprocity with the living world, receiving the gifts with open eyes and open heart.” – Robin Wall Kimmerer, Braiding Sweetgrass 
Noticing the abundance that surrounds us and practicing gratitude is powerful. Join us as we cultivate our awareness and appreciation for the many gifts of the Earth – the air we breathe, the water we drink, the food we eat. How might we reciprocate? As we deepen our connection with Mother Earth, we strengthen our commitment to protect her. 
“Attention is the beginning of devotion.” – Mary Oliver 
This immersive afternoon nature connection retreat will enliven your senses as you slow down, linger in liminality and calm your weary mind. Together, we will explore natural pathways to homeostasis and equilibrium that will help us navigate life’s ups and downs, as well as the upcoming holiday season. 
Your guide, Christa Hebal, will lead you on a peaceful saunter through the fall forest, weaving mindfulness, breathwork, forest bathing and nature therapy together for a restorative afternoon on some of the trails less traveled at the North Carolina Arboretum. We’ll celebrate the experience in community, enjoying a special wild-foraged tea ceremony and snacks. Bring an open mind and an open heart. All are welcome. Presented through Adult & Continuing Education Programs in collaboration with Asheville Wellness Tours. 
Christa Hebal is a certified Nature and Forest Therapy Guide by the Association of Nature and Forest Therapy. Born and raised in the mountains of northeast Tennessee, she has lived in Asheville for 24 years. Christa has an adventurous heart, and loves to help others encounter wholeness through embodiment and nature connection practices. She has had a professional bodywork practice for 18 years as a nationally certified Massage Therapist, and is also a practitioner of Ortho-Bionomy®, Usui Reiki Master, Certified Pediatric Massage Therapist, Clinical Aromatherapist, and Certified Traditional Herbalist. She is also certified in CPR and Wilderness First Aid.

title: Get Down in the Field- Ecstatic Dance Waves w/ Sara Bensman
description:
Asheville Movement Collective
Sunday, November 8th
1st Dance Wave 8:30\-10:30am \| Warmup 8:30am \| Opening Circle 9am
2nd Dance Wave 10:30\-12:30am \| Warmup 10:30am \| Opening Circle 11am
Facilitator Sara Bensman

Intention: Get Down in the Field

There’s evidence that before humans could speak, we made music. Since we have walked the earth, we have likely danced. We dance together to share community, to alchemically transmute our internal experiences, to celebrate, to mourn, to communicate, and to simply enjoy the sensation of music moving through our bodies. In the sharing of this practice, we sometimes experience a deep connection to the room of dancers, even a sense of Oneness in which the tight hold that wraps around our individual ego begins to loosen and we feel the entirety of the Collective Field. We marvel at the variation of forms and unique movements that are aspects of the one great orchestration of the universe and recognize that I am that and that is me. This dance is an invitation to shift our internal lenses to the widest aperture and focus our awareness of the Collective Field.

## About Sara Bensman

Sara’s mix-making arises from musical exploration. She seeks to understand energy through somatic responses to sonic vibrations. Her facilitation is propelled by a desire to help build and sustain community by creating a safe, loving container for self-expression, connection and release. If you’d like to listen to her sets visit [https://soundcloud.com/sara-bensman](https://soundcloud.com/sara-bensman)

title: Grateful Vibrations:A Complimentary Sound Appreciation Gathering
description:
Star Sounds Asheville
## About the event

### A Special Gathering of Cosmic Vibrations, Connection & Celebration

**A Complimentary Sound Journey at Compassionate Expressions in Leicester, NC**
Come gather, connect, and celebrate the cosmic vibrations within us all!
You're invited to a very special Star Sounds experience at **Compassionate Expressions**, a beautiful, spacious venue nestled in Leicester.
Since arriving in Asheville during the pandemic, I've dedicated myself to creating immersive sound journeys and sharing the language of the stars with our mountain communities.
Over the years, many attendees have described these experiences as truly one of a kind. I typically bring seven magnificent gongs, Tibetan singing bowls, crystal bowls, a handpan, and an assortment of unique sound instruments to create a deeply immersive journey.
But the magic isn't simply in the instruments.
**It's in what happens within you when you give yourself the space to listen, feel, and discover.**
And this gathering has something extra special in store!

### A Little Cosmic Timing

We'll begin with an Evolutionary Astrology transmission exploring the powerful journey of **Venus Retrograde**, as she prepares to turn **direct** on **November 12**.
Venus invites us to examine what we value, how we love, what we cherish, and how authentically we express ourselves.
What have we discovered during her journey through the underworld? What are we ready to reclaim, release, or bring back into the light?
From there, we'll move into a **60-minute immersive Star Sounds Journey**, allowing the vibrations to carry us beyond the noise of everyday life and into the mystery of our own being.
Afterward, we'll simply sit in the bliss, connect, share, and appreciate the unique vibrations each of us brings into the room.

### And There's Another Special Ingredient...

A talented professional videographer and friend, who has experienced many of my gatherings, has offered to film this event.
We're not putting on a show. We're simply going to gather, be ourselves, and let the magic unfold naturally. We will pretend he's not in the room.
After the journey, those who feel inspired will have an opportunity to share their experience through a brief video testimonial.
No scripts. No rehearsals. Just your authentic expression.
Participating in a testimonial is entirely optional, and we'll make sure everyone understands the filming arrangements before we begin.
My hope is that these moments will help share the essence of Star Sounds with others who have yet to experience it.

**Going??? Be sure to bring a Pad or Mat and a water bottle**

### A Gift of Gratitude

**This entire event is FREE!**
As a thank-you for your presence and support, we'll also hold a raffle for several complimentary **Evolutionary Astrology readings, valued at $144 each.**
My intention with every Star Sounds gathering is that you leave with something to ponder, something to feel, and perhaps something you hadn't recognized within yourself before.
**Knowing more about yourself, from yourself.**
I don't create these experiences to tell you what to discover. I create space for more to be revealed.
And what reveals itself is uniquely yours.
**Because authentic expression isn't about becoming something more. It's about allowing more of who you already are to emerge.**

I don't know when we'll have another gathering quite like this, so come celebrate with us. Bring a friend, bring your curiosity, and bring your own beautiful vibration.
**Let's make some magic together!**
With gratitude,
David
*Star Sounds \| Evolutionary Astrology & Immersive Sound Journeys*

title: Exhibition on Screen | The Danish Collector: Delacroix to Gauguin
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
For many years no-one was interested in the art of the Impressionists. Artists like Monet, Degas and Renoir were vilified, attacked, and left penniless as a result. Then, something remarkable happened. A new breed of collectors emerged and, before long, they were battling to acquire any work by these new, radical artists that they could find. Amongst them was the visionary Danish businessman Wilhelm Hansen. It was an extraordinary moment in art history; full of drama, intrigue and subterfuge. Some collectors we may recognize and some we may not, but Hansen amassed a remarkable collection housed at his summer home, Ordrupgaard, on the outskirts of Copenhagen. Exhibition on Screen tells his fascinating story and, with exclusive access to a sell- out exhibition at London’s Royal Academy, brings the extraordinary collection to the big-screen in glorious high-definition. From Hansen’s beautiful house and gardens at Ordrupgaard to the streets of bohemian Paris, this film takes you on a journey to discover some of the best examples of 19th-century French art ever collected. 
Purchase Tickets

title: Fantasy and Sci-Fi Silent Book Club
description:
Asheville Introverts
BOYB - Bring Your Own Book and rant or rave about your current Fantasy or Sci-fi titles!

**What is a Silent Book Club?**
Referred to as "Introvert's Happy Hour", Silent Book clubs allow readers to engage with each other without the commitment of reading a shared title. Community members gather in the same place, have some casual chit chat, and then read silently together. **This group will focus on Fantasy and Sci-Fi titles (subgenres & related genres are welcome!)**

**How does it work?**
For the first 15-30 mins we will gather, grab drinks and engage in introductions. Feel free to discuss your recent favorites, mention a title that lives in your head rent free, or ask for recommendations! The best part of the Silent Book Club is being able to talk shop with other readers!

Once settled in we will dedicate 45 minutes to silent reading. Your book can be traditional, ebook, or audiobook. Read at your own pace!

Afterwards we will go around show-and-tell style and share what we read with the group. We want to know what you're reading! Organic dialogue welcome!
