title: New Moon Ceremony
description:
Senseful Soul’s Asheville Healing Community🧘🏻‍♀️🏳️‍🌈🪐🔮
Join us for a gathering to set new intentions and connect with the energy of the new moon.
Meet the New Moon in ceremony through astrology, Akashic soul journeying, ritual & embodied intention.
Approaching the threshold of a new lunar cycle with intentionality is a powerful choice that becomes even more amplified when done in community.

The New Moon offers a monthly portal to pause, listen inward, and consciously seed what you desire to cultivate in the cycle ahead. Gathering in ceremony creates the space to step outside the momentum of everyday life and meet that threshold with presence, allowing your intentions to be witnessed, embodied, and amplified within the collective.

Each New Moon also carries the unique energetic signature of the zodiac sign it moves through, offering different themes and invitations for your growth. By working intentionally with the astrology of each lunation, you can align your intentions with the energies already available to you and receive deeper clarity around what is ready to begin.

Each month, we gather at the Soul Sanctuary beneath the dark moon sky for an evening of astrology, soul journeying, ritual, and embodied intention.

**This month with the Scorpio New Moon, we invite you beneath the surface, into the places where truth, power, intimacy, and transformation reside.**

**Together, we’ll work with Scorpio’s alchemical medicine to release what has run its course, reclaim energy or power we’ve given away, and plant intentions rooted in the deeper truth of who we are becoming.**

**What to Expect**

* Guided drop-in meditation
* Astrological teaching + transmission
* Guided Akashic soul journey
* Reflection + intention setting
* Ceremonial fire offerings
* Closing embodiment + integration
* Sacred space for connection and community

No prior experience with astrology, meditation, or ceremonial practice is necessary. Simply come as you are.

**About Your Facilitators**
Alessandra Mary is a trained priestess, ceremonialist, and Akashic guide devoted to creating spaces where the sacred becomes something you can experience, embody, and weave into everyday life.

Jenn is a witch of the cosmos and astrologer who brings the language of the stars down to earth, illuminating the energetic patterns and possibilities available within each lunar cycle.

Together, Alessandra and Jenn weave the mystical and the embodied, the cosmic and the ceremonial, creating a space where you can not only understand the energy of the New Moon, but more importantly, experience it.

**What to Bring**
Our ceremony will primarily take place outside on the grass around the fire, with a large covered porch available as our rain plan. Please dress with the evening weather in mind.

**Be sure to bring:**

* Water bottle
* Journal + pen
* Comfortable clothing and layers appropriate for the weather
* Any sacred objects, crystals, talismans, or other items you would like to place on our collective altar and charge during the ceremony

Lawn blankets and meditation cushions will be provided, though you are very welcome to bring your own blanket, cushion, or camping chair if you’d prefer.

Come ready to slow down, listen deeply, sit beneath the dark moon, and lean into what is waiting to begin.

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: Shut Up & Write event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

HOSTS: This is a multi-host event, so most of the time there will be a host present. If we are unlucky and no host can attend, please find each other and self-organize. Pay attention to the event chat and comments to see who is available.

WI-FI: Yes!

PARKING: Street parking in metered spots is free after 6pm. Closest municipal garages ($2/hour) are Wall St. & Coxe Street/Sears Alley.

title: A Connecticut Yankee in King Arthur’s Court - Mark Twain
description:
Books That Age Like Wine
**Mark Twain moves from broad comedy to biting social satire in this literary classic.**

**Cracked on the head by a crowbar in nineteenth-century Connecticut, Hank Morgan wakes to find himself in King Arthur’s England. After using his knoweldge of an upcoming solar eclipse to escape a death sentence, Hank must then navigate his way through a medieval world whose idyllic surface masks fear, injustice, and ignorance.**

**Considered by H. L. Mencken to be “the most bitter critic of American platitude and delusion…that ever lived,” Twain enchants readers with a Camelot that strikes disturbingly contemporary notes in this acclaimed tour de force that encompasses both the pure joy of wild high jinks and deeply probing insights into the nature of man.**

title: Weave Kudzu Vines Into a Basket
description:
Weave Kudzu Vines Into a Basket
with Carleigh Fairchild 
Wednesday, November 11  |  10am – 4pm 
Register Here!
Turn wild vines into a basket in this hands-on kudzu weaving workshop. Kudzu, often thought of as an invasive plant, offers a surprising gift: strong, flexible vines that make for beautiful, functional baskets. In this workshop you’ll learn how to identify, harvest, and prepare kudzu responsibly, turning an abundant wild plant into a useful basket. Together we’ll explore weaving techniques and create baskets that reflect each of our creativity. Come away with your own handmade basket, practical knowledge for future projects, and a new appreciation for kudzu. There will be a 30 minute lunch break and materials will be provided. If you have sharp pruners, feel free to bring them along! 
Carleigh Fairchild has a deep love for the Earth. She gardens, keeps bees, wild harvests, processes animals, tans hides, weaves baskets, and finds joy in time spent around the fire. As the founder of Human Nature Connection LLC, she is dedicated to helping others rediscover respectful and collaborative relationships with the more then human world. Carleigh’s journey—including 86 days on the survival show ALONE in Patagonia—deepened her understanding of belonging and connection. With over 25 years of experience, she teaches both online and in-person classes in Western North Carolina, weaving together earth skills, community, and healing. Carleigh is also a NIASZIIH bodywork healer and instructor at Wilderness Fusion, integrating body, earth, and spirit in her practice.

You're invited to a special evening at Little Jumbo called Conversations About Inspiration on November 11th from 6:30 - 8:30 pm.

This project is born out of my long-time marriage to musician and composer, Alan Hall. I'm fascinated and mystified that his artistic inspiration comes in the form of sound and rhythm. As a wordsmith, mine is sparked by words.

Bring your portfolio, case study, or work in progress on your laptop, tablet, or phone.

Experienced professionals from UX, design, research, and product will be available to provide feedback on:

* Visual presentation and structure
* Problem framing and communication

Reviewers will circulate throughout the event, offering individual feedback and opportunities for discussion. Attendees can also exchange ideas, share their work, and learn from one another.

Designers, researchers, product managers, developers, founders, students, career-switchers, and anyone interested in UX and product design.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: The Sound of America
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
AmiciMusic returns with a thrilling program entitled “THE SOUND of AMERICA.” Pianist and Artistic Director Daniel Weiser will be joined by violinist Tim Schwarz from Philadelphia in this exciting exploration of the incredible diversity of our American sound.  The program includes Spirituals and Ragtime as well as Blues-inspired works by W.C. Handy and William Grant Still, the Native-American inspirations of Charles Cadman, the Jewish influence on Ernest Bloch, the country fiddling in Aaron Copland, and the Latin rhythms in Bernstein’s West Side Story.  Weiser and Schwarz served as the 1996 U.S. Artistic Ambassadors of Music for which they performed more than 50 concerts in 11 countries in the Middle East and Southeast Asia showcasing our American music. 
AmiciMusic is a chamber music organization based in Asheville and Baltimore dedicated to performing the highest quality chamber music in intimate venues and non-traditional spaces. This concert breaks down barriers between performers and audiences by setting up a more relaxed and informal atmosphere through informative talks about each composer’s life before each piece is played. 



Add a VIP Ticket: Round out your concert experience by joining us from 5:45–6-45pm in the Museum’s Perspective Café for a pre-concert reception. Meet the musicians and your fellow concert goers while enjoying a drink and some light bites. Premium reserved seating for VIP ticket holders will allow you to join the concert just before start time. 
About the Musicians
Since his solo debut with the legendary Philadelphia Orchestra at age nine, violinist Timothy Schwarz has had a brilliant career as a soloist, chamber musician, and pedagogue. Praised for his “energetic performances” (Rome News) and “technique beyond reproach” (Buffalo Times), Schwarz regularly performs throughout Europe, Asia, and the Americas as a soloist and chamber musician. His many recordings include the 2018 release of Anthems from Prometheus (Albany Records) “All credit to Timothy Schwarz for providing a performance as gripping from first to last as this one” (Fanfare Magazine), the 2013 release of Early Chamber Works by Jennifer Higdon (Naxos) “Top 10 Classical Albums in 2013” (Philadelphia City Paper) and his 2006 release of Timothy Schwarz, Live! “Good enough to be the only recording in your collection” (American Record Guide).  An avid educator, Schwarz is currently Assistant Professor and Head of Strings at Rowan University and Artistic Director and Founder of Techne Music, which includes a summer chamber music camp and concert series. For a five-year period through 2001, Schwarz served three tours as Artistic Ambassador in South America, Asia, and Africa, performing over 100 recitals in 15 countries. He received a Masters of Music from the Peabody Conservatory and a Doctorate of Musical Arts in Performance from Temple University. For further information and a performance schedule, visit www.TimothySchwarz.com. 
Daniel Weiser, pianist, has a Doctorate in Piano/Chamber Music from the Peabody Conservatory, where he studied with Samuel Sanders and Robert MacDonald and won the Richard Franko Goldman prize for outstanding contribution to musical and educational life. He has performed on many great stages, including the Weill Recital Hall of Carnegie Hall, the National Gallery of Art in Washington D.C., and on the Dame Myra Hess Concert Series in Chicago. He has also concertized around the world, including Israel, Thailand, Holland, and France and was the 1996 United States Artistic Ambassador Abroad, for which he performed on an eleven-country tour of the Middle East and Asia. He has been on the music faculty of Dartmouth College and the prestigious St. Paul’s School in Concord, New Hampshire.

title: Handmade Holiday: Clay Gingerbread Cookie Monsters
description:
Handmade Holiday: Clay Gingerbread Cookie Monsters
with Eileen Bos 
Friday, November 13  |  11 am – 2 pm 
Register Here!
Using Sculpey Polymer Clay, we will soften and roll the clay out with a rolling pin, and use gingerbread cookie cutters to begin our creature creations… each cookie creature will have hand painted glass eyes to install, and we will use pre-colored polymer clay to add decorations, creating buttons & details to help bring them to life! They can be made into ornaments, magnets, pins, etc. They can even sit upright & be glued to the top of a cookie jar for future Christmas cookies! All materials will be included in this class. 
Eileen Bos is a multimedia sculpture artist from NY, with nearly 40 years of self-taught art experience. She began drawing at the age of 3 and sculpting at age 4. She has competed in The Nickle City cake Challenge, was featured on the cover of Buffalo Magazine, won several tablescape awards at Bride’s World Events, showcased in an ad in NYC’s Times Square, and much more! Along with art, Eileen has a deep love of Quantum Sciences & Metaphysics and is working on developing art classes that fuse hands-on arts with Metaphysical principles to help people learn, heal & grow in exciting, multifaceted ways. You can find her work at: www.enchantedartwork.com.

title: Naturalist Walk & Talk
description:
Naturalist Walk and Talk
with Shane Myers 
Friday, November 13  |  1 – 3 pm 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
Walk around the Arboretum with our staff naturalists and talk about what we see around us. We might see plants and animals, and evidence of them going about their lives in our backyard. Topics will be based on what we see and experience and whatever questions that come up, so every class has the potential to be quite different. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Shane Myers’ interest in nature began as a child with a love of dinosaurs. He’s assisted in outreach and education for plant conservation groups, Odonata Groups, and various bird groups. Shane currently works for the Adult Education department at the NC Arboretum.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: The Plate Scrapers
description:
"They make a classic bluegrass sound that's not afraid to go somewhere new." —Appalachian Jamwich




Born from the tradition of bluegrass jams & potlucks, THE PLATE SCRAPERS — Derek Kretzer (banjo), Andrew Jordan (guitar), Robbie Mann (fiddle), Jody Mosser (dobro), and Kevin Johnson (bass) — have been putting in the work and showcasing their love for the genre since 2014. They’ve since released 3 studio albums, 3 live albums, and have toured relentlessly up and down the east coast and into the midwest. 



In 2019, they won the Podunk Bluegrass Telefunken Band Contest. They have been featured on WAMU Bluegrass Country Radio, performed as an IBMA Official Showcase artist, and their latest release, "Destination Horizon" (2020) debuted at #9 on the Bluegrass Album Billboard charts with rave reviews from Bluegrass Today. 



As a progressively-minded bluegrass band that strives to maintain a healthy equilibrium between their diverse musical backgrounds and traditional Appalachian sounds, they’ve wowed audiences across the entire spectrum, truly feeling at home on any stage. 



They’ve provided direct support for bluegrass legends such as The Seldom Scene, Frank Solivan & Dirty Kitchen, and Larry Keel. On the other side of that coin, they aren’t afraid to get weird at a late night festival slot and have become well known for their tastefully balanced and refreshingly diverse songwriting. 



Catch their live show and you’ll be sure to receive a full helping of hard-driving bluegrass favorites and heart-wrenching country ballads!

title: Choose Between a 5 KM/3.1 Mile and a 10 KM/6.2 Mile Guided Waynesville Walk
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
We will be joining the Asheville Amblers, AARP, the Cardinals Elite Walking Team, and perhaps some others for this event. Registration is at 9:30 a.m. with step-off at 10:00. The walk is free, although the Amblers do accept donations (suggested donation $4.00).

Meet in front of Mast General Store, 63 N. Main St., Waynesville NC 28786. The walks go past public art, Civil War sites, along the Waynesville Greenway, and more. The 10 KM walk adds Town Hall, the historic Frog Level area, nice neighborhoods, and a peaceful cemetery with spectacular views.

Note: the 5 KM walk will be at a slightly slower pace. The 10 KM walk will be at a slightly faster pace.

There are some hills, so some may want walking poles (I will be taking both of mine); sneakers should be fine. Dogs are welcome. Strollers should be ok, though it will require one or two work-arounds. Bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Dress appropriately for the weather.

Parking is easier a block to either side of Main Street. Mast General Store doesn't have a public restroom, but we can direct you to one nearby should you need it.

Many people go out to eat together after this walk at places like Sweet Onion and Angelos. You will want to shop at Mast General Store and several other downtown shops. The last time we did this walk, people were asking about the availability of ice cream and chocolates.

Why not make a day of it!

Swannatopia Presents: BOOM BOOM BARNS is a free, all ages, ambient farm stroll and multimedia light show to be held on November 14, 2026 at Warren Wilson College. description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.



Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.

Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
Coworking for writers in your area!
Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.

Please arrive a few minutes early to say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.

Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!

A note about the format
We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.

description:
Join us for an afternoon of music and art in the Museum. With a soundscape of piano music, we invite you to experience artwork in the galleries in a more emotional and sensory way. 
ABOUT THE MUSICIAN
Diego Vázquez is a Spanish pianist from Madrid now based in Asheville, NC, who views music as a way to understand and express emotions beyond words. He began playing at age four and developed a strong classical foundation, later expanding into pop and musical theater. After years of studying in Spain, he now pursues music independently in the U.S., performing as a chapel pianist, choir member, and orchestra musician while also learning the organ. His cross-cultural journey shapes a deeply expressive style, with music focused on connection rather than perfection.

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers! 🌟
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**. 🍺🎮

🔥 **Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death! 🤪

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.

title: Shut Up & Write!® - Downtown
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

**Other Important Details:**

***\*\*\*Please note: Shut Up & Write event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

HOSTS: This is a multi-host event, so most of the time there will be a host present. If we are unlucky and no host can attend, please find each other and self-organize. Pay attention to the event chat and comments to see who is available.

WI-FI: Yes!

PARKING: Street parking in metered spots is free after 6pm. Closest municipal garages ($2/hour) are Wall St. & Coxe Street/Sears Alley.

title: Blue Ridge Ecosystems – From Ice Age to the Present
description:
Blue Ridge Ecosystems – From Ice Age to the Present
with Dan Lazar 
Wednesday, November 18  |  1 – 3pm 
BRN – Core  |  BREG – Elective 
Register Here!
Blue Ridge ecosystems have changed dramatically since the end of the last ice age 18,000 years ago.  For example, while glaciers still covered northern Ohio and Pennsylvania, the summits of the Great Craggy Mountains, the Black Mountains and the Smokies were treeless and clothed in alpine tundra vegetation, while Mastodons and Giant Ground Sloths roamed the valleys below.  As the climate warmed, the plant and animal communities we see today slowly developed. 
Dan Lazar served for many years as the director of education at the Western North Carolina Nature Center, followed by several years as executive director of the Colburn Earth Science Museum. Dan has a degree in forest biology from the State University of New York College of Environmental Science and Forestry and has been an instructor in the Blue Ridge Naturalist program since 2005.

Asheville Young Professionals (AYPROS)
**An entire section reserved for AYPROS. A special shoutout during the game. A group photo ON THE COURT afterward. And tickets are just $5.**
We're teaming up with UNC Asheville Athletics for a special AYPROS Night at Kimmel Arena on **Wednesday, November 18**, and this is one you won't want to miss.

Whether you're a die-hard Bulldogs fan or haven't been to a game in years, this is a pretty great excuse to get out, meet some new people, and show some love for our hometown team.

The Bulldogs will be taking on the **Tennessee Tech Golden Eagles**, and there's even more to look forward to than just the game! Between the game, our reserved section, the in-game recognition, and the chance to get everyone together on the court afterward, this is shaping up to be a pretty special night. We'll share more details as we get closer, but for now, get your tickets, find something blue to wear, and help us give the Bulldogs a proper home-court advantage!
**Tickets are only $5 (normally $25) with our exclusive AYPROS discount code.** That's a night of Division I college basketball, reserved seating with our crew, a special in-game recognition, and a chance to be part of a photo on the court afterward for less than the price of most coffees. Plus, plus, plus...

### Game Day Details

* **Date:** Wednesday, November 18, 2026
* **Time:** 6:30 PM
* **Location:** Kimmel Arena at UNC Asheville
* **AYPROS Seating:** Section 6
* **Tickets:** Just $5 with promo code **AYPROS**
* **What to Wear:** Your best BULLDOGS BLUE! We want to see a sea of blue in our section and in our group photo.

### How to Get Your $5 Tickets

1. Click **[Purchase Your AYPROS Tickets Here](https://university-of-north-carolina-asheville-ilh9.vivenushop.com/event/6a79dfcabe06b62435059128/6ab535875a3b4d739107f1a1)**.
2. Select "Buy Tickets" and enter promo code **AYPROS** when prompted.
3. Choose your seats in Section 6 and complete your purchase.

We've reserved Section 6 specifically for AYPROS, and we'd love nothing more than to fill it! Tickets are available directly through UNC Asheville Athletics, so be sure to purchase yours and encourage your friends to do the same.
**One last thing: DON'T FORGET TO WEAR BLUE!** If we're going to get recognized in front of the arena and take a group photo on the court, we might as well look like we belong there.
A huge thank you to **Kassi Butcher and the UNC Asheville Athletics team** for helping put this special evening together for AYPROS.

title: Gratitude: Connecting with the Heart Through Creative Expression
description:
Gratitude: Connecting with the Heart Through Creative Expression
with Catherine Willows 
Thursday, November 19  |  10 am – 1 pm 
Register Here!
In the depths of autumn, Thanksgiving invites a pause—to step outside the momentum of everyday life, connect with your heart, and open to the energy of gratitude. Gathering together in the Arboretum gardens, we’ll attune to the natural world of the season and the quiet wisdom within. Gratitude is more than something you think about or name. It is an energy, a quality of presence, a frequency. When you pause long enough to connect with it, something shifts—awakening a greater receptivity to the richness of what is here, to what has touched and nourished you, and to what is quietly ready to be revealed. 
Through intuitive painting, guided reflection, and expressive art-making, we’ll explore gratitude through color, imagery, symbols, and words. Noticing what catches your attention and allowing the creative process to lead, space opens for what is within to become visible, felt, or known in its own way. 
No artistic experience is needed, only curiosity, a willingness to listen inwardly, and an openness to discover what reveals itself. All art materials will be provided. 
Catherine Willows is a Registered Nurse, Certified Functional Medicine Health Coach, and Transformational Creativity Coach, and founder of Willows Coaching and Consulting. While holding sacred space, she guides adults in awakening their inner creativity — moving beyond the demands of daily life into greater flow, self-discovery, and joy through intuitive art-making processes. Catherine believes creativity and our connection to the natural world are deeply interwoven — both vital pillars of wellbeing, supporting nervous system regulation and inner equanimity, and together essential for living a meaningful, embodied life aligned with purpose and authentic expression.

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

What to Bring: Valid photo ID and proof of Henderson County residency (like a recent utility bill, lease agreement, or official mail with your current address).

No appointment necessary. You can visit the pantry during regular operating hours. Service is generally provided on a first-come, first-served basis.

The Process: Volunteers will greet you, help you with a brief registration, and provide you with a selection of fresh and non-perishable food items.

description:
Beginning Botany
with Alexandra Holland 
Friday, November 20  |  1 – 4pm 
BRN and BREG Core 
Register Here!
It’s a tough life for a plant: make dinner, create and nurture offspring, fight off predators, deal with the neighbors. In Beginning Botany we’ll explore how plants handle these daily challenges using and modifying only leaves, stems, and roots. We’ll cover the basics of plant structure and function. 
Alexandra Holland has a passion for getting people excited about the natural world through classes, hikes, and photography.  She graduated from Duke University and earned her master’s degree in botany from the University of Texas at Austin.  While in Texas, Alexandra managed the UTEX Culture Collection of Algae at UT Austin and volunteered with education programs at the Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center.  Upon moving to Asheville, she began volunteering with the NC Arboretum’s youth education programs.  In 2008 she was in the first class of students to be certified as Blue Ridge Naturalists.   Alexandra teaches botany classes at the NC Arboretum and leads nature hikes in Western NC for groups of all ages.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: Without Shade, Without Rest Film Screening and Discussion
location: Kittredge Arts Center, Kittredge Theater
description:
Join us November 20, at 6pm in Kittredge Theater for a screening of the film Without Shade, Without Rest. There will be light refreshments provided and a discussion of farm and food worker rights following the film. 

 

WeCount! is a non-profit, human rights organization that represents immigrant workers and families in South Florida, including plant nursery workers. WeCount!’s advocacy on extreme heat is the subject of the new documentary, Without Shade, Without Rest by Six Eye Films and Working Films. This documentary tells the story of two organizations, WeCount! and the Coalition of Immokalee Workers, and our efforts to win heat protections for Florida’s outdoor workers. In the face of intense industry lobbying and aggressive state preemption, the fight in Florida continues. Their work has helped put extreme heat in the national conversation and inspired advocacy for workplace heat standards across the country. 

 

While “Without Shade, Without Rest” is primarily focused on Florida, we believe this film can be a helpful tool for workers, advocates, organizations, and community members across the country and world, who are similarly grappling with the growing and existential threat of climate change and extreme heat. We hope the film helps shine a light on an urgent labor and human rights issue and contributes to meaningful dialogue and connections across our movements. In Asheville, a new campaign Planting Justice (Sembra Justicia) is being launched by WeCount! and local partners in support of workers in the house plant industry who work locally with little labor protections. The food we eat and the plants we enjoy are nothing without the workers who plant and nurture them.

title: See the Sights of Cherokee on a 10 KM/6.2 mile Walk
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
We'll gather at the Welcome Center across from the fairgrounds. Our route takes us past the Museum of the Cherokee People and the Qualla Arts and Crafts facility. We then walk the road up to the *Unto These Hills* Amphitheatre. From there we pass the Oconaluftee Indian Village and walk through the Botanical Gardens. Coming back down the back way, we loop around ending up at the Oconaluftee Islands Park with its "bamboo forest." From there we return to the start point.

Hiking boots are not needed, though some will want walking poles. (I plan to take both of mine.) Do bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Dress for the weather. I'm not sure whether dogs are allowed in the Botanical Gardens, but it is a short loop and if necessary, you can walk around the parking lot for the few minutes it will take us to make that loop. While much of this walk is on pavement, trail strollers would be needed for the walk, with a few workarounds.

Drive into Cherokee on US-441. When you pass the Cherokee movie theater, the highway will turn left. Look for the fairgrounds on your left and the Welcome Center on your right. We will gather in the parking lot. There are restrooms in the Welcome Center.

title: Mammals of the Southern Appalachians
description:
Mammals of the Southern Appalachians
with Carlton Burke 
Saturday, November 21  |  12 – 4pm 
BRN – Core  |  BREG – Elective 
Register Here!
The rugged mountains of Appalachia host a tremendous variety of mammal species ranging from tiny shrews weighing only a few ounces at most to huge mammals such as the black bear which can weigh in at several hundred pounds. Also large mammals such as the cougar, bison, and elk also once commonly roamed these mountains. In this class we will discuss present and past mammals of the region, their distribution, natural life cycles, and also controversies and cultural connections they have with the ever increasing human population of the area.  Class participants will also have a chance to meet a few live, native mammal species of the mountain region as well. 
Carlton Burke is a naturalist and educator who operates Carolina Mountain Naturalists, an educational service which offers wildlife and nature educational programs throughout western North Carolina. He also was on the staff of the western North Carolina Nature Center in Asheville for over 25 years as the Curator of Exhibits. Carlton co-hosts a weekly radio program NATURE NEWS and is also a NC state and federally licensed wildlife rehabilitator.

title: NOBODY'S DARLING STRING BAND
description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.



Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.



The five women comprising Nobody’s Darling each have a long history of playing old-time music. Individually they have played in many other bands through the years, including The Carolina Oldtimers, The Pegtwisters, The Zuma House Band, Too Hot To Cook, The Luke Smathers Mountain Swing Band, Honey Holler, and The Carolina Chick Peas.



Stop in to enjoy the music and an afternoon libation or two, perhaps with an early supper or light bite . . . and don't forget your dancing shoes!

title: Jackson Grimm's Old Time Machine
description:
Jackson Grimm marries folk pop melodies with the lonesome sound of traditional Appalachian music. 



His Appalachian-infused Americana songs run the gamut from a traditional country waltz homage ("If Not For You") to an unrequited love song driven by a Beatles-esque melody ("I'd Hold You, But I Don't Wanna Hold You)" to a drunken Old Crow Medicine Show-style partygrass number ("Last Train Home").



Grimm studied Traditonal Music at Warren Wilson College under the tutelage of renowned players like Wayne Erbsen and Kevin Kehrberg. He also studied guitar, banjo, mandolin & singing with the Western North Carolina music master, Josh Goforth.



He also plays extensively as a sideman for his father, singer-songwriter Tim Grimm, touring all over the US and to Europe. Jackson has appeared on, written songs on, and co-produced the last two Tim Grimm albums. He's has also shared the stage and played with singer-songwriters Ben Bedford, Krista Detor, Jennie DeVoe & Old Sap.



Still a hometown boy, Grimm can be found playing solo or around Western North Carolina with Holler Choir, One Stringband, or his Old Time Machine.



Music 8:30-11:30pm, $10 cover at the door.

title: Shut Up & Write - South Asheville
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
Coworking for writers in your area!
Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.

Please arrive a few minutes early to say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.

Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!

A note about the format
We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.

For our full event schedule, visit https://shutupwrite.com

Other Important Details:

Venue Guidelines: Please thank our hosts by purchasing something.

title: Exhibition on Screen | The Danish Collector: Delacroix to Gauguin
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
For many years no-one was interested in the art of the Impressionists. Artists like Monet, Degas and Renoir were vilified, attacked, and left penniless as a result. Then, something remarkable happened. A new breed of collectors emerged and, before long, they were battling to acquire any work by these new, radical artists that they could find. Amongst them was the visionary Danish businessman Wilhelm Hansen. It was an extraordinary moment in art history; full of drama, intrigue and subterfuge. Some collectors we may recognize and some we may not, but Hansen amassed a remarkable collection housed at his summer home, Ordrupgaard, on the outskirts of Copenhagen. Exhibition on Screen tells his fascinating story and, with exclusive access to a sell- out exhibition at London’s Royal Academy, brings the extraordinary collection to the big-screen in glorious high-definition. From Hansen’s beautiful house and gardens at Ordrupgaard to the streets of bohemian Paris, this film takes you on a journey to discover some of the best examples of 19th-century French art ever collected. 
Purchase Tickets

title: Walk the Eastern End of Maggie Valley Starting at McCracken Corner Park
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Meet at McCracken Corner Park, 56 State Rd 1307, Waynesville 28785 (Moody Farm Road/State Road 1307 intersects Soco Road twice; this is the eastern intersection with a traffic light further from Maggie Valley). We will meet at 2:00 p.m.

**Note: There is no restroom at the start point. Our route will pass a convenience store, and there is a restroom about halfway through the walk at Parham Memorial Park. Please plan accordingly.**

Dress for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen. The walk is pretty flat, all on pavement except for a short portion near the end. Tennis shoes are fine; walking poles aren't needed (although I plan to bring one). Bring plenty of water and a protein snack. Dogs are welcome. Strollers are fine.

We will walk up Soco Road to Parham Memorial Park (the western intersection of Moody Farm Road/State Road 1307 and Soco Road). Then we will walk along Moody Farm Road, with one short side excursion, back to the start point.

Hope to see you there!

Open to all levels, whether you're new to this or have been practicing for years.

title: OLD-TIME JAM
description:
The roots of Appalachian old-time music stretch far across the Atlantic and we're proud to honor and showcase that legacy at Jack of the Wood Pub with our long-running Old-Time Jam sessions — every Wednesday starting at 5pm! Recently recommended by Rolling Stone for "those looking for an organic, participatory [music] experience" in Asheville, the Old-Time Jam is one of several weekly traditional jam sessions hosted at JACK.

title: Weekly Critique
description:
AVL Writers
This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.

For our group discussion, please bring at least 8-10 printed copies of your piece. That way, we can all read through each other's work and provide feedback.

Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.

If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.

If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: NOBODY'S DARLING STRING BAND
description:
Nobody’s Darling String Band plays lively music in the old-time tradition at Jack of the Wood Pub every Saturday afternoon from 4-6pm.



Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.



The five women comprising Nobody’s Darling each have a long history of playing old-time music. Individually they have played in many other bands through the years, including The Carolina Oldtimers, The Pegtwisters, The Zuma House Band, Too Hot To Cook, The Luke Smathers Mountain Swing Band, Honey Holler, and The Carolina Chick Peas.



Stop in to enjoy the music and an afternoon libation or two, perhaps with an early supper or light bite . . . and don't forget your dancing shoes!

Sunday, November 29th
1st Dance Wave 8:30\-10:30am \| Warmup 8:30am \| Opening Circle 9am
2nd Dance Wave 10:30\-12:30am \| Warmup 10:30am \| Opening Circle 11am
Facilitator Ted Riskin

## About Ted Riskin

Ted is interested in anything that can get him out of his head, and music and movement do a pretty good job of that. He hopes to offer music that facilitates an inner journey and invitations that create a shift. While he likes modern electronic music, he can’t create a mix without including lots of natural instruments and voices. Due to a short attention span, he mixes in lots of different musical genres. You can hear some of his mixes on [https://www.mixcloud.com/tarisk/](https://www.mixcloud.com/tarisk/)

description:

Most of us carry a voice that second-guesses, criticizes and quietly undermines — not just how we see ourselves, but how we see everyone around us. It picks at faults, sets impossible expectations and convinces us we're not enough. Left unchecked, that voice doesn't just damage our confidence — it sabotages our happiness, our relationships and our ability to grow.

title: Let's Walk at Lake Junaluska
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
Gather at 2:00 at Lake Junaluska inside the Bethea Welcome Center. This will be a 7 KM/4 mile route. The walk does not just go around the lake, but through the Nature Garden, along the Rose Walk, and up to Lambuth Inn. The view from Inspiration Point is a must-see!

Dress for the weather. Consider a hat and sunscreen. Some people may want walking poles, especially for the walk up to Lambuth Inn; tennis shoes should be fine. It is particularly important that walkers bring a protein snack and **plenty of** **water**. Restrooms are available at the Welcome Center, at Lambuth Inn, and along the route. Dogs on leash are welcome. Strollers are ok.

title: Game Night @ Archetype Brewing
description:
Asheville's Bored Game Geeks
tldr: \*\*We are at Archetype Brewing - West!\*\* Bring your favorite game(s) or learn a new one – members are always happy to teach! See you there and have a blast!

🎲🍻 **Welcome to the Game Night Extravaganza!** 🍻🎲

Calling all dice-rollers, card-shufflers, and strategy-curious adventurers! 🌟
Are weeknights feeling a tad mundane? Fear not! We’ve got the antidote: **Board Games, Brews, and Bliss**. 🍺🎮

🔥 **Our Mission:** To ignite laughter, forge alliances, and maybe—just maybe—unleash a few friendly rivalries & battle to the death! 🤪

No PhD in rulebooks required! Whether you’re a Settlers of Catan enthusiast or a Code Names solving ninja, or your first time touching a board game ***we will explain all the rules needed.*** 🏰🎉

Expect:

* **Beer on Tap**: Because rolling dice is better with a pint in hand.
* **Low Brainpower Required**: We’re all about fun, not Fermat’s Last Theorem.
* **Epic Showdowns**: Ticket to Ride routes, Splendor gem heists, and High stakes Camel Up.

Feel free to request any game you’d like to play or bring your own. So gather your guild, stack your resource cards, and let the games begin! May your laughter be loud, your moves be bold, and your victory dances be legendary. 🎭🎲
See you at the table! 🌟🍻

**Feel Free to bring your own games too!**

title: Birding for Beginners
description:
Birding for Beginners
with Shane Myers 
Tuesday, December 1  |  9 – 10:30am 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
Join us on this birding walk around the NC Arboretum gardens and trails in search of our most colorful residents. We will go over best practices for using binoculars, recommendations for purchasing your own binoculars, and popular field guides to use. Bring your own binoculars but if you do not have a pair we have some loaner binoculars available to use during the programs. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Shane Myers’ interest in nature began as a child with a love of dinosaurs. This quickly grew to include fossils, insects, and reptiles, and learning from the notes his grandparents kept of the birds that came to their feeders in Toledo, Ohio.  He has a Bachelors of Science in Wildlife Biology and did most of his undergraduate work on dragonflies and damselflies. He’s assisted in outreach and education for plant conservation groups, Odonata Groups, and various bird groups. Shane currently works for the Adult Education department at the NC Arboretum. 
●  Members: Remember to enter your promo code upon checkout to receive your 10% member discount! Email adulteducation@ncarboretum.org with questions. 
●  See a full listing of Adult Education Programs at the North Carolina Arboretum here! Questions? Check our FAQs. 
●  We are committed to fostering a diverse, supportive learning community. If the cost of a class is a barrier for you, please complete this scholarship form and we will see what kind of assistance we can provide.

title: AVL Digital Nomads - Book Club
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**December 2026 Selection - *When Breach Becomes Air* by Paul Kalanithi**
[Amazon](https://www.amazon.com/When-Breath-Becomes-Paul-Kalanithi/dp/081298840X/) - [GoodReads](https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/25899336-when-breath-becomes-)

*At the age of thirty-six, on the verge of completing a decade’s worth of training as a neurosurgeon, Paul Kalanithi was diagnosed with stage IV lung cancer. One day he was a doctor treating the dying, and the next he was a patient struggling to live. And just like that, the future he and his wife had imagined evaporated. When Breath Becomes Air chronicles Kalanithi’s transformation from a naïve medical student “possessed,” as he wrote, “by the question of what, given that all organisms die, makes a virtuous and meaningful life” into a neurosurgeon at Stanford working in the brain, the most critical place for human identity, and finally into a patient and new father confronting his own mortality.*

*What makes life worth living in the face of death? What do you do when the future, no longer a ladder toward your goals in life, flattens out into a perpetual present? What does it mean to have a child, to nurture a new life as another fades away? These are some of the questions Kalanithi wrestles with in this profoundly moving, exquisitely observed memoir.*

*Paul Kalanithi died in March 2015, while working on this book, yet his words live on as a guide and a gift to us all. “I began to realize that coming face to face with my own mortality, in a sense, had changed nothing and everything,” he wrote. “Seven words from Samuel Beckett began to repeat in my head: ‘I can’t go on. I’ll go on.’” When Breath Becomes Air is an unforgettable, life-affirming reflection on the challenge of facing death and on the relationship between doctor and patient, from a brilliant writer who became both.*

\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-\-

**Welcome to our monthly Book Club!** We’re a small, friendly group that gets together for fun, thoughtful conversations about a different book each month.

Finished the whole book? Great. Only made it through a few chapters? Still come. Didn’t read it at all but the discussion sounds interesting? Honestly, you’re welcome too.
We meet on the **first Tuesday of every month**.

One of the best things about this group is that we keep it relatively small and guide the conversation, so it doesn’t turn into three people talking while everyone else quietly questions their life choices. Everyone has a chance to jump in, share their thoughts, and explore the book’s characters, themes, writing, and bigger ideas.

You definitely don’t need to be a literary expert. Whether you read constantly or you’re trying to get back into it, this is a relaxed place to discover new books, hear different perspectives, and meet some great people along the way.

title: Handmade Holiday: Wild Ornaments
description:
Handmade Holiday: Wild Ornaments
with Carleigh Fairchild 
Wednesday, December 2  |  10 am – 1 pm 
Register Here!
Using cattail leaves and colored ribbons we will make several different styles of ornaments: animal shapes and star shapes. 
Previous basket making or weaving experience is not necessary but you will use fine motor skills to make these ornaments. You will have the opportunity to make many during our time together, to decorate your tree or to give as gifts. All materials are provided in this class. 
Carleigh Fairchild has a deep love for the Earth. She gardens, keeps bees, wild harvests, processes animals, tans hides, weaves baskets, and finds joy in time spent around the fire. As the founder of Human Nature Connection LLC, she is dedicated to helping others rediscover respectful and collaborative relationships with the more then human world. Carleigh’s journey—including 86 days on the survival show ALONE in Patagonia—deepened her understanding of belonging and connection. With over 25 years of experience, she teaches both online and in-person classes in Western North Carolina, weaving together earth skills, community, and healing. Carleigh is also a NIASZIIH bodywork healer and instructor at Wilderness Fusion, integrating body, earth, and spirit in her practice.
